newsitem.title: USA: GM to recall Cadillacs in Calif. settlement.
newsitem.headline: GM to recall Cadillacs in Calif. settlement.

text.p: General Motors Corp said it has agreed to recall 44,000 Cadillacs for an emissions repair and will make payments totaling $1.1 million as part of a settlement deal with the California Air Resources Board.

The settlement resolves claims that the 4.9-liter V-8 engine used in 1991-1993 Cadillacs exceeded California's limits for carbon monoxide emissions when the cars' air conditioning systems were running.
The agreement is similar to a 1995 settlement betweeen GM and the U.S. Environmental Protection agency covering Cadillacs equipped with the 4.9-liter engines in other states.

Although GM maintains that the cars never violated any emissions laws, it agreed to voluntarily recall the cars. The automaker said it has already repaired about 60 percent of the 44,000 cars in California and about 60 percent of the 470,000 of the cars in other states.

The 30-minute repair involves installing new software into the car's engine control module to bring the cars into emissions compliance when their air conditioners are running. GM no longer produces the 4.9-liter engine in question.
Also under the settlement, with the California Air Resources Board (CARB), GM said it will:
-- Remit a $600,000 payment to the California Air Pollution Control Fund.
-- Donate $500,000 to help finance University of Southern California studies on the effects of air pollution on children's health.

-- Loan three GM EV1 electric vehicles and three electric Chevrolet S-10 pickup trucks to the board for six years. GM will upgrade two of the EV1s and one S-10 with nickel-metal-hydride battery packs when such batteries are introduced commercially by GM.
